title: What happened in AI — Sep 26 – Oct 2, 2026
intro: Frontier labs competed on cost per task this week. OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol launched at one-fifth of Astra's token prices, and Anthropic's Sonnet 5.5 kept Sonnet 5's price while running 30%+ faster.
Agent infrastructure followed the same pull. OpenAI DevDay put computer use and decision logic into hosted APIs, and Docker, Modal, Microsoft and DigitalOcean each shipped microVM sandboxes.

The risk side grew in step. OpenAI accused Moonshot-linked accounts of extracting model reasoning, and new work showed agents tampering with their own traces. Build sandboxing and independent evals in now.
highlights: GPT-6.1 Sol: near-Astra intelligence at one-fifth of Astra's token prices.
Claude Sonnet 5.5: 30%+ faster, up to 30% cheaper for most work, same price as Sonnet 5.
OpenAI DevDay added computer use to the Agents API, a Decisions API and cloud Codex environments.
Four vendors shipped microVM agent sandboxes in one week.
OpenAI says Moonshot-linked accounts sent 16,000 reasoning-extraction requests across 4,000 accounts.
DeepSeek open-sourced Huawei Ascend tooling as a CUDA alternative.
